newsitem.title: USA: Campo sees charge, CEO stepping down.
newsitem.headline: Campo sees charge, CEO stepping down.

text.p: Campo Electronics, Appliances and Computers Inc said Monday Anthony Campo was stepping down as chairman and chief executive officer, and the company would take a "significant restructuring charge" in the quarter ended February 28.
It said its board had accepted Campo's offer to step down and had named President and Chief Operating Officer Rex Corley as acting chairman and chief executive.
Anthony Campo will remain a member of the board.

Campo said it recently closed two stores -- in Jackson, Miss., and Huntsville, Ala. -- to improve performance. It said it plans to announce a significant restructuring charge for the second quarter ended February 28, which will include the effects of the store closings, among other things.
The amount of the restructuring charge has not yet been determined, it said.

L. Ron Forman, a member of the board, said, "Over the past two years, the performance of the company has been in a steady decline. While our problems reflect an industry-wide slump, the board believed that the time had come to set a new direction for the company."

He said, "The board believes that prompt action is important, and, to that end, is actively engaged with its new management team in a thorough assessment of the company's operations. A number of options are under consideration by the company in order improve its sales performance, liquidity and profitability, and fundamental changes are certain.
"We expect an orderly management transition, and appreciated the cooperative efforts shown by all involved as we get on with the work of restoring the company's financial position."
An Executive Search Committee has been formed to conduct a nationwide search for a permanent chairman and chief executive officer. Corley is expected to be a candidate for the positions.
"I am in total agreement with the board that it's time to take this company in another direction," said Anthony Campo.
